cells.v: Knockback, Launch Speed, Hitstun, Hitlag & Shieldstun Calculation for P+ 3.1.5
You can also mouseover the bolded title of the attribute to view the description

A character's resistance to knockback. Keep in mind the actual factor used is 100+Weight. This means that at the same percent, Jigglypuff takes 218/160=1.36x as much knockback as Bowser, instead of 118/60=1.97x (not counting Base Knockback)
-- The line between Marth and Diddy Kong represents who falls down from Fox's (Grounded) Shine.

A character's vertical acceleration while airborne. It is always downward. The only times an airborne character is not accelerating by this amount is while airdodging, during certain specials, or while falling faster than max fall speed.
The lower the value, the more easily the fighter slides along the ground. Closely related to wavedash length.
How much the character can accelerate horizontally while airborne. A-Mobility scales with how far you tilt the stick, while B-mobility activates in full once the stick leaves the deadzone.
The angle the character falls at after reaching max velocity, both horizontally and vertically. Measured from vertical (0° is straight down, 90° is sideways)
A character's acceleration while dashing. Related to how noticeable their moonwalk is.
The acceleration a character experiences when their current airspeed (horizontally) exceeds their max H air Speed. It also applies when you're moving through the air and your stick is neutral.
The max speed a character can reach by drifting. Most characters can reach a higher airspeed (usually by run->jump), in which case they will gradually slow down to reach their Max H Airspeed.
The distance a character travels when doing a max angle wavedash.
The length of both the forward and backward glide tosses each character has. Direction (Forward/Backward) is determined by which way you roll, not which way you throw.
-- I highlighted in black characters that can spawn their own items.
The length of each characters' longest possible DACUS. I also included Squirtle's RHUS (RAR JC Usmash)

cells.note:
A character's resistance to knockback.

The line between Marth and Diddy represents who falls down from Fox's Shine.

Keep in mind the actual factor used is 100+Weight. This means that at the same percent, Jigglypuff takes 218/160=1.36x as much knockback as Bowser, instead of 118/60=1.97x (not counting Base Knockback)

A character's vertical acceleration while airborne. It is always downward. The only times an airborne character is not accelerating by this amount is while airdodging, during certain specials, or while falling faster than max fall speed.
Whenever a character is airborne, they are accelerating downward until they reach this velocity.
When a fast-fall is initiated, the fighter instantly reaches this speed.
The difference between a character's maximum fall speed and their fast fall speed.
The (approximate) height achieved by a character's jump from the ground.
Multijump characters are represented by white-on-black text.
How high characters go during a walljump. Note that walltech jumps (PassiveWallJump) are the same as normal walljumps.
This is the angle of a perfect, max-angle wavedash. A perfect waveland (with the control stick full horizontal) has a slightly longer distance.

An "Extended Dash Dance" is when a character dashes and holds forward until the last frame possible to avoid entering run. The dash animation continues, although it slows down since the stick is neutral. For standardization, this value is taken in 20 frames, instead of the length of the dash animation, which varies by character.

This is the number of frames it takes for a character to reach their maximum run speed from their initial dash speed. Negative frames indicate that the character decelerates from their initial dash speed to their maximum run speed.

This is distance it takes for a character to reach their maximum run speed from their initial dash speed. For characters which slow down to their maximum speed, this indicates how far it takes for them to decelerate to their maximum speed.
This is the speed the character has at the start of their dash.

This is the ability of the character to alter their speed during the dash animation.
A-mobility scales with the control stick's position, while B-mobility is applied in full once the stick leaves the deadzone.
This is really only important for characters whose run speed is faster than their initial dash speed, such as sonic.
This also is related to moonwalking.
This is the speed a character has while in a full Run.
Also known as traction.
The speed when a character is walking as fast as possible. Related to wavedash length (see the wavedash calc page for more)
The max air speed a character can reach just by drifting. If they reach a speed higher than this (usually by run-jump) they will slow down, as determined by their air drag.
The ability for a character to accelerate horizontally while airborne. A-mobility scales with the control stick's position, while B-mobility is applied in full once the stick leaves the deadzone.

This is the acceleration a character experiences when:
1. They are moving faster than their Max Airspeed.
2. They are moving horizontally at all and their control stick is neutral.
This is the angle from vertical the character falls at once they've reached their Max H Airspeed and Max fall speed.

Distance gained by doing a dacus of maximum length.
A distance of less than 20 generally means the distance gain is negligible compared to a simple running Usmash.
I also included Squirtle's max-length RHUS (RAR JC Usmash).
Since DACUS is a 2-frame window, some characters go farther with the earlier input, while some go further with the later input. see the dacus sheet for more.

Distance gained by a max-distance Glide Toss.
White-on-black means that character can spawn in items which can be GT'd.
The distance the character moves when they do a max distance boost grab, measured on the first frame the grab is active. Grab range is not accounted for.
Characters below the line get knocked down by Fox Shine

cells.v: Initial Velocity is taken from animation
This is the last frame of the Dash animation on which you can hold forward without entering Run.
Dropping Shield is actionable on frame 15.
Airdodge (Wavedash) has a landing lag of 10 frames.
In addition each character has 2 hidden alts by holding R or Z while going from the CSS to SSS
* Ike can only walljump with his SideB, Quickdraw
* Knuckles can only wallcling and climb with his SideB, Glide
Frame data for techs is universal across the cast.
JC Grabs have (minimum) one extra frame of startup compared to standing grabs.
Be aware of this when comparing Dash Grabs and JC Grabs.
Boost grabs also have at least one extra frame of startup.
This is measured from the center of the character, not the outermost hurtbox
100+ Attack also has a stronger hitbox frames 50-51
This is the frame data pertaining to each  characters' 4 Ledge Options: Stand(Climb), Roll, Jump, and Attack.
This does not pertain to anything performed by dropping from the ledge, such as a ledgedash.
Vulnerable is the first frame when the character can be hit. Intangibility lasts from frame 1 to the frame before this.
Ledge is the first frame another player can grab the ledge.
SAF, or Soonest Actionable Frame is the first frame the player can start another action.
Hit is the frames the hitboxes are active during CliffAttack.
Note on Colors: Green is always higher values, regardless of whether or not a higher value is advantageous.
For the Jump Action: Vulnerable, Ledge, and SAF are always the same frame.
I'm not going to put the details of every Attack hitbox here but in general:
- 7-11 DMG; >100% attacks usually do more damage
These values do not include the character's jumpsquat, or Empty landing lag (See MISC)
Values may change by 1 or 2 frames depending on the animation the character is in before landing
Meta Knight's aerial throws cannot be interrupted with an air special or airdodge until frame 31, 31, 30 and 26 respectively
Lucario's aerial throws are "glitched." Every throw makes him turn around again, meaning F, U, and D turn him around, but B does not.
ASDI can move you an extra 3 units left/right, full SDI will move you 6 for every input.
Ground to Air Jump Momentum Multiplier
Projectile Weapon Use F Dash Speed
Projectile Weapon Use B Dash Speed
Terminal Velocity Frames for Hard Landing
XRotN Bone (bone to be grabbed from?)
Default Vertical Position of Pause Camera
This acts as a 'no-jank' value. Ike and Samus have different values to account for Quickdraw and the Super Wavedash (not sure about Kirby).
cells.note: Oddly enough, it does not seem to limit the Run Speed, although it does limit nearly everything else (including the dash animation)

cells.v: In Project M, this is the Powershield Size Multiplier
This is how much airspeed you get from tilting the stick when you jump.
Your Current speed is multiplied by this before being factored into your initial airspeed
Initial Airspeed is capped by this. It applies whenever you jump or slide off an edge. It does not apply when you drop through a platform.
Controls Double Jump Height for most characters (not DJC or multijump)
No clue what this does. Increasing it seems to have no effect
Air Mobility A scales with how far you tilt the stick, B activates in full when the stick is not in the deadzone.
Technically the Max H airspeed. Mobility can only accelerate you to this speed, 0x080 will slow you down if you're moving faster than this.
Another 'no-bugs' value. Applies when double-jumping; possibly at other times as well.
All translation values in all animations are multiplied by this.
AKA Why Jiggs' Shield Break is so special
These are applied the frame invincibility wears off during a ledgejump (slow and fast)
These are all pretty useful to know. L-canceled value is this -1, divided by 2, rounded down, +1
These control both normal walljumps and walljump-techs
If it is true, the throw animation has a constant frame speed modifier of (victim's weight /100)

cells.v: The color represents whether initial dash speed or run speed is higher, which determines how their distance is calculated.
If initial speed is higher, they slow down according to their friction
If Run speed is higher, they speed up according to dash acceleration. (column BC)
If initial = run speed, then their speed is constant.
While wavedashing, your traction is doubled while you're moving faster than your Max Walk Speed.
